details: A suspected $6.3 billion hack on Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has sent shockwaves through the crypto markets, causing widespread selling and significant liquidations. The breach, which began with a $296 million XRP drain after 36 hours of preparation, led to approximately $1.57 billion in forced liquidations across various cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin, Ethereum, and numerous altcoins experienced notable declines, with the total crypto market capitalization falling 3-4%. Binance has stated it is working to freeze stolen assets, with help from industry partners, and has allocated over $6.34 billion from company funds to cover potential losses. Investigators have also uncovered additional breach points beyond an initially suspected compromised employee laptop, and North Korea's TraderTraitor group is believed to be responsible. Despite Binance's efforts, the incident has severely shaken investor confidence.
title: Binance Hack Triggers $6.3 Billion Loss & Market Sell-Off

details: Ethereum (ETH) has seen a net outflow exceeding $1 billion from US spot Ethereum ETFs throughout October, signaling persistent institutional de-risking. This comes despite a significant net withdrawal of approximately 169,770 ETH (worth around $407 million) from centralized exchanges in one day in late October, marking the largest such withdrawal in over four months. While large exchange withdrawals can indicate accumulation and reduced sell-side supply, the substantial ETF outflows present a conflicting signal, leaving ETH without a clear directional catalyst in the short term. Analysts are closely watching whether ETF redemptions continue or reverse to gauge future market direction for Ethereum.
title: Ethereum ETFs Face Over $1 Billion in October Outflows

details: Bitcoin's price dipped significantly, testing key support levels around $76,000-$77,000, following the Binance hack and a broader sell-off in technology stocks. Earlier in the week, Bitcoin had briefly surged past $81,800, reaching a session high of $81,888, driven by stronger-than-expected third-quarter U.S. GDP data. However, the enthusiasm was short-lived, as news of the Binance breach quickly reversed these gains, pushing the cryptocurrency down by over $2,500. The $75,000 level is now considered a critical support, with a sustained break below it potentially opening the door to further downside.
title: Bitcoin Tests Key Support After Binance Hack & Tech Sell-Off
